questions.question: In February 2025, five cheetahs were released into which national park of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuno National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In February 2025, five cheetahs were released into **Kuno National Park**, located in **Madhya Pradesh**, India.
 
• This release is part of India's ambitious **Cheetah Reintroduction Project**, aimed at reintroducing cheetahs in the country after their extinction nearly 70 years ago.
 
• The cheetahs were translocated from Africa as part of a collaborative effort between India and countries like **Namibia and South Africa**.
 
• Kuno National Park was selected for this project due to its suitable habitat, abundant prey base, and minimal human-wildlife conflict.
 
• This effort is a step toward restoring ecological balance and ensuring the conservation of endangered species in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuno National Park**

 
 
• Located in the **Sheopur district of Madhya Pradesh**, Kuno was declared a national park in **2018**.
 
• The park spans over an area of approximately 748 square kilometers and is known for its diverse flora and fauna.
 
• Kuno was originally considered a potential site for relocating Asiatic lions from Gir National Park in Gujarat.
 
 
 
• **Cheetah Reintroduction in India**
 
 
• **Cheetahs were declared extinct in India in 1952 due to habitat loss**, hunting, and human interference.
 
• The current reintroduction plan is the first time wild cheetahs have been translocated across continents.
 
• The project involves collaborative efforts with Namibia and South Africa, where the cheetahs were sourced.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance of Cheetahs**
 
 
• Cheetahs are apex predators, playing a critical role in maintaining the balance of ecosystems.
 
• Their presence helps control herbivore populations, promoting the growth of vegetation and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of the Project**
 
 
• Ensuring the survival and adaptation of cheetahs to their new environment is a significant challenge.
 
• Potential risks include poaching, human-wildlife conflict, and insufficient prey base in the area.
 
• Continuous monitoring, habitat management, and public awareness are crucial for the project's success.

questions.question: Which of the following authorities was strengthened in 2024 to enforce penalties and green clearances under India’s environmental regulations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Pollution Control Board**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2024, the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** was given enhanced powers to enforce penalties and ensure compliance with environmental regulations in India.
 
• The CPCB operates under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) and is the apex body for pollution control in the country.
 
• The amendments empowered the CPCB to impose stricter fines and oversee the implementation of green clearances to address environmental violations effectively.
 
• As part of its expanded role, the CPCB was tasked with ensuring adherence to environmental standards by industries, urban bodies, and other entities.
 
• The move aimed to strengthen India's capacity to tackle air, water, and soil pollution, ensuring sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB):**

 
 
• Established in 1974 under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act.
 
• It also functions under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981.
 
• The CPCB advises the central government on environmental policies and coordinates with state pollution control boards.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Clearances in India:**
 
 
• Green clearances are required for activities that may have significant environmental impacts.
 
• These include projects in sectors like mining, infrastructure, and energy.
 
• The process is overseen by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) and the CPCB.
 
 
 
• **Pollution in India:**
 
 
• India faces challenges related to air pollution, water contamination, and waste management.
 
• According to the World Air Quality Report, several Indian cities rank among the most polluted globally.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• Goal 13 focuses on climate action, while Goal 15 emphasizes sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems.
 
• Strengthening environmental regulations aligns with India's commitment to achieving these goals.

questions.question: What is India's Human Development Index (HDI) value in the 2025 Human Development Index Report?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.685**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's Human Development Index (HDI) value for 2025 is projected to be **0.685**, as per the Human Development Index Report.
 
• The HDI is a composite index measuring average achievement in three basic dimensions of human development: **health, education, and standard of living**.
 
• India's HDI has been steadily improving due to consistent progress in **life expectancy, literacy rates, and per capita income**.
 
• India is classified as a country with **medium human development**, given its HDI value falls between 0.550 and 0.699.
 
• Despite improvements, India continues to face challenges such as **inequality, regional disparities, and low gender equality**, which impact its overall HDI ranking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**

 
 
• HDI is published annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in its Human Development Report.
 
• The index focuses on three dimensions: **health (life expectancy), education (mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (GNI per capita).**
 
• It ranges from 0 to 1, where a higher value indicates better human development outcomes.
 
 
 
• **India's HDI Trends**
 
 
• India's HDI value has seen consistent growth over the last few decades due to government initiatives in health, education, and poverty alleviation.
 
• For instance, India's HDI value was **0.645 in 2019**, and it has shown an upward trend despite challenges like the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
 
 
• **Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)**
 
 
• IHDI accounts for inequality in the distribution of each dimension of HDI.
 
• India's IHDI value is typically lower than its HDI value, highlighting inequality in education, health, and income.
 
 
 
• **Global HDI Context**
 
 
• In the latest Human Development Report, countries like **Norway, Ireland, and Switzerland** rank highest in HDI.
 
• India's HDI ranking is typically around the **130-140 range**, reflecting its medium level of human development compared to global peers.

questions.question: What significant financial commitment was agreed upon during the extended session of COP16 in Rome?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**$200 billion annually for biodiversity conservation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the extended session of **COP16 **in **Rome**, member nations agreed to allocate **$200 billion annually** for biodiversity conservation.
 
• This financial commitment aims to address the ongoing global biodiversity crisis, including habitat loss, species extinction, and ecosystem degradation.
 
• The funding will support initiatives like **restoration of ecosystems, protection of endangered species**, and sustainable management of natural resources.
 
• The decision aligns with the objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) to protect 30% of the planet's land and marine areas by 2030, also known as the "30x30" target.
 
• Countries were encouraged to mobilize resources from both public and private sectors to meet this ambitious goal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD):**

 
 
• An international treaty adopted in 1992 at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro.
 
• Aims to conserve biodiversity, promote sustainable use of its components, and ensure fair sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources.
 
• The CBD has been ratified by 196 nations, making it a globally recognized framework for biodiversity protection.
 
 
 
• **30x30 Target:**
 
 
• A global initiative to protect at least 30% of Earth's land and ocean areas by 2030.
 
• Proposed under the Global Biodiversity Framework to halt and reverse biodiversity loss.
 
• Focuses on safeguarding key biodiversity hotspots and ecosystems critical for climate regulation.
 
 
 
• **Global Biodiversity Crisis:**
 
 
• According to the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES), over 1 million species are at risk of extinction.
 
• Major drivers include deforestation, climate change, pollution, and overexploitation of natural resources.
 
• Urgent action is necessary to prevent irreversible damage to ecosystems and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Funding Mechanisms:**
 
 
• Countries are urged to mobilize financial resources through mechanisms like green bonds, biodiversity trust funds, and public-private partnerships.
 
• International organizations like the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and Green Climate Fund (GCF) play a pivotal role in financing biodiversity initiatives.

questions.question: In February 2025, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs extended the deadline for private companies to dematerialise their securities. What is the new deadline?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30 June 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)** in India extended the deadline for private companies to dematerialise their securities to **30 June 2025**.
 
• Dematerialisation is a process wherein physical certificates of securities are converted into electronic form.
 
• This extension was announced in February 2025 to provide private companies with adequate time to comply with regulations.
 
• The previous deadline for dematerialisation of securities was set earlier but has been extended for better implementation and compliance.
 
• Private companies are required to ensure their securities are held in electronic form through a depository participant registered with SEBI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dematerialisation of Securities:**

 
 
• Dematerialisation eliminates the risks associated with holding physical certificates, such as loss, theft, or forgery.
 
• Securities in electronic format are managed through depositories like NSDL (National Securities Depository Limited) and CDSL (Central Depository Services Limited).
 
• It facilitates easier transfer, trading, and monitoring of securities.
 
 
 
• **Depository Participant:**
 
 
• A Depository Participant (DP) acts as an intermediary between the investor and the depository.
 
• Registered with SEBI, DPs provide services like opening demat accounts, transferring securities, and holding securities electronically.
 
 
 
• **SEBI's Role:**
 
 
• The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates securities markets in India and ensures compliance with dematerialisation guidelines.
 
• SEBI mandates dematerialisation to promote transparency and efficiency in the trading of securities.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Dematerialisation:**
 
 
• Ensures safe storage and easy transfer of securities.
 
• Helps reduce paperwork and administrative costs associated with physical certificates.
 
• Enhances market liquidity and facilitates faster settlement of transactions.

questions.question: How many launches of the LVM-3 rocket are planned for the Chandrayaan-4 mission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Chandrayaan-4 **mission by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is planned to have **two launches using the LVM-3 rocket**.
 
• The **LVM-3** (Launch Vehicle Mark-3) is ISRO's heaviest and most advanced launch vehicle, capable of carrying **payloads up to 8,000 kg to Low Earth Orbit **(LEO).
 
• The two launches will ensure the deployment of the required mission components, which may include an orbiter, lander, and rover, depending on the mission design.
 
• The Chandrayaan-4 mission is expected to build on the advancements made during the Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3 missions, focusing on lunar exploration and scientific research.
 
• ISRO uses the LVM-3 rocket for critical missions due to its high reliability and capability to handle complex payloads.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **LVM-3 Rocket (Launch Vehicle Mark-3):**

 
 
• The LVM-3, previously known as **GSLV Mk-III**, is a three-stage heavy-lift launch vehicle developed by ISRO.
 
• It has a lift-off mass of approximately 640 tons and stands 43.5 meters tall.
 
• The rocket uses a combination of solid, liquid, and cryogenic propulsion systems.
 
• LVM-3 is also the launch vehicle for India’s human spaceflight program, Gaganyaan.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan Missions:**
 
 
• Chandrayaan-1 (2008): India’s first lunar mission focused on mapping the Moon’s surface and detecting water molecules.
 
• Chandrayaan-2 (2019): Aimed at soft-landing a rover on the lunar south pole, though the lander lost communication during descent.
 
• Chandrayaan-3 (2023): Successfully demonstrated soft-landing and deployed a rover for lunar surface exploration.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Objectives of Chandrayaan-4:**
 
 
• To further explore the lunar surface, particularly the unexplored south pole region.
 
• To conduct advanced experiments on lunar geology, topography, and surface composition.
 
• To test new technologies for future interplanetary missions.
 
 
 
• **ISRO's Lunar Exploration Roadmap:**
 
 
• ISRO plans to establish a strong presence in lunar exploration as part of its long-term goals.
 
• Future missions include more advanced lunar landers and potential collaboration with international space agencies.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the new Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) in December 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**V Ramasubramanian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shri Justice V Ramasubramanian**, former Judge of the Supreme Court of India, assumed the charge of the **Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission**.
 
• The NHRC is tasked with protecting and promoting human rights in India, including rights related to life, liberty, equality, and dignity.
 
• **Justice V Ramasubramanian**** succeeded** **Justice Arun Mishra**, who previously held the position of NHRC Chairperson.
 
• Justice Arun Mishra is known for delivering several landmark judgments during his tenure at the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The appointment of the NHRC Chairperson is made by the President of India based on recommendations from a committee comprising the Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Leaders of Opposition in both Houses, and the Union Home Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)**

 
 
• Established on October 12, 1993, under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
 
• It is a statutory body tasked with investigating complaints of human rights violations and ensuring their protection.
 
• The NHRC can recommend corrective measures and compensation for human rights violations but does not have judicial powers.
 
• It has powers of a civil court for summoning, examining witnesses, and requisitioning public records during inquiries.
 
 
 
• **Composition of NHRC**
 
 
• NHRC consists of a Chairperson, four full-time members, and seven ex-officio members.
 
• The Chairperson must be a retired Chief Justice or Judge of the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Other members include experts in law, human rights, and public administration.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Contributions of Justice Arun Mishra**
 
 
• Known for interpreting laws related to land acquisition, environment, and constitutional provisions.
 
• Played a key role in delivering judgments impacting corporate governance and public interest.
 
 
 
• **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993**
 
 
• This Act provides for the establishment of NHRC and State Human Rights Commissions.
 
• Defines "human rights" as rights related to life, liberty, equality, and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or international covenants.

questions.question: India Infoline Finance Limited (IIFL Finance), India’s leading non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), has rebranded how many of its existing branches as all-women staffed ‘Shakti’ branches to mark Women’s Day (8 March 2025)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India Infoline Finance Limited (IIFL Finance) is one of India’s leading non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) offering diversified financial services.
 
• On the occasion of Women’s Day (8 March 2025), IIFL Finance rebranded **seven of its existing branches** as all-women staffed ‘Shakti’ branches.
 
• The ‘Shakti’ branches aim to promote women empowerment by creating an inclusive workplace environment and serving as centers for women-led financial services.
 
• These branches are staffed entirely by women and are designed to provide financial products and services tailored to women entrepreneurs and customers.
 
• The initiative emphasizes IIFL Finance’s commitment to gender diversity and the empowerment of women in the financial sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs):**

 
 
• NBFCs are financial institutions that provide banking services without meeting the legal definition of a bank.
 
• They offer products such as loans, asset financing, and investment products but cannot accept demand deposits like savings accounts.
 
• NBFCs play a critical role in financial inclusion, especially in rural and underserved areas.
 
 
 
• **Women Empowerment in Finance:**
 
 
• Empowering women in the financial sector includes promoting gender diversity, leadership roles, and equal opportunities.
 
• Initiatives like all-women branches encourage women’s participation in economic decision-making.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Women’s Day:**
 
 
• International Women’s Day, celebrated annually on March 8, highlights the social, economic, cultural, and political achievements of women.
 
• The day is also a call to action for accelerating gender parity and women’s rights worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Financial Products for Women:**
 
 
• Several financial institutions offer customized products for women, including lower interest rates on loans and exclusive savings accounts.
 
• These products aim to encourage women’s entrepreneurship and financial independence.

questions.question: What is the IMF’s revised global growth forecast for 2025 as per IMF’s April 2025 Global Financial Stability Report?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.8%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the **IMF's April 2025 Global Financial Stability Report**, the revised global growth forecast for 2025 is **2.8%**.
 
• The IMF slightly adjusted its global economic outlook due to **persistent inflationary pressures** and **geopolitical uncertainties**.
 
• Developing economies are expected to contribute significantly to global growth, with a stronger rebound in sectors like manufacturing and services.
 
• Advanced economies are predicted to experience slower growth due to **tightening monetary policies** and **sluggish consumer demand**.
 
• The revised forecast reflects a cautious optimism, with the IMF emphasizing the need for **structural reforms** to sustain long-term economic resilience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF):**

 
 
• Established in 1944, the IMF aims to foster global monetary cooperation, secure financial stability, and promote sustainable economic growth.
 
• It publishes the Global Financial Stability Report biannually to analyze the stability of global financial markets and emerging risks.
 
 
 
• **Global Growth Trends:**
 
 
• Global growth rates fluctuate based on factors like inflation, trade policies, geopolitical conflicts, and technological advancements.
 
• Growth projections are essential for policymakers to plan fiscal and monetary interventions.
 
 
 
• **Inflationary Pressures:**
 
 
• Inflation impacts consumer purchasing power and overall economic activity, influencing growth forecasts.
 
• Central banks often adjust interest rates to manage inflation and stabilize economies.
 
 
 
• **Structural Reforms:**
 
 
• Reforms like enhancing labor market flexibility, improving infrastructure, and reducing trade barriers can boost long-term growth potential.
 
• Such measures are pivotal for emerging markets aiming for sustainable economic development.

questions.question: What is India's rank in Transparency International's 2024 Corruption Perceptions Index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**96th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India ranked **96th** in Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) for the year 2024.
 
• The CPI measures perceived corruption in the public sector across 180 countries and territories using expert assessments and opinion surveys.
 
• Countries are scored on a scale of 0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean); India's score has been improving gradually over the years.
 
• India’s ranking reflects its ongoing efforts to combat corruption and improve transparency in governance.
 
• Denmark, Finland, and New Zealand typically top the CPI rankings as the least corrupt countries globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transparency International:**

 
 
• An independent, non-governmental organization focused on combating global corruption.
 
• Founded in 1993, headquartered in Berlin, Germany.
 
• Publishes the annual Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) to highlight corruption trends globally.
 
 
 
• **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI):**
 
 
• Ranks countries based on perceived levels of public sector corruption as scored by experts and businesspeople.
 
• Uses data sources from organizations like the World Bank, World Economic Forum, and others.
 
• Higher scores indicate lower levels of corruption; lower scores indicate higher corruption levels.
 
 
 
• **India's anti-corruption initiatives:**
 
 
• Implementation of laws like the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Lokpal Act.
 
• Promotion of digital governance to reduce bureaucratic corruption.
 
• Efforts to increase transparency in public procurement and financial transactions.
 
 
 
• **Global perspective:**
 
 
• Countries like Somalia and Syria often rank at the bottom of the CPI due to weak governance and systemic corruption.
 
• Strong institutions, freedom of press, and public access to information are key factors for higher CPI rankings.

questions.question: In April 2025, India launched a strategic initiative to boost its defence exports by offering low-cost loans to countries traditionally reliant on Russian arms. Which Indian institution is primarily responsible for facilitating these loans?

options.text: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank)** is a specialized financial institution established in 1982 under the Export-Import Bank of India Act, to promote and facilitate India's international trade and investment.
 
• EXIM Bank plays a pivotal role in extending **concessional credit lines** and loans to partner countries, particularly in strategic sectors like defense exports.
 
• In April 2025, India launched a strategic initiative to boost defense exports by offering low-cost loans to nations traditionally reliant on Russian arms, facilitated primarily by EXIM Bank.
 
• EXIM Bank's efforts align with the Indian government’s “**Aatmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India)**” initiative, aiming to reduce dependency on foreign imports and strengthen domestic defense manufacturing.
 
• The institution also promotes India’s exports by providing financial support, including buyer’s credit, supplier’s credit, and export project finance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aatmanirbhar Bharat in Defense**

 
 
• The Indian government has been actively promoting self-reliance in defense manufacturing by encouraging indigenous production of arms, ammunition, and equipment.
 
• India aims to become a major exporter of defense equipment, reducing its reliance on imports from countries like Russia and the US.
 
• In 2020, the government introduced a list of items banned for import to boost domestic defense production.
 
 
 
• **Role of EXIM Bank in International Trade**
 
 
• EXIM Bank provides financial assistance for exports and imports of goods and services, as well as investments in foreign countries.
 
• It supports Indian exporters by offering credit at competitive rates, making Indian products more attractive in international markets.
 
• The bank also facilitates India’s soft power diplomacy by providing concessional credit to developing countries for infrastructure and other projects.
 
 
 
• **Defense Exports from India**
 
 
• India’s defense exports have been growing steadily, with a focus on exporting items like missiles, radar systems, and patrol vessels.
 
• Key markets for Indian defense exports include Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Middle East.
 
• The Indian government aims to achieve defense export targets of ₹35,000 crore by 2025 under the "Make in India" initiative.
 
 
 
• **Other Institutions Involved in Defense Financing**
 
 
• While EXIM Bank is the primary institution for facilitating defense export loans, other institutions like the State Bank of India (SBI) may also play a supporting role by offering additional financial services.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) provides regulatory oversight for such financial initiatives to ensure compliance with monetary policies.

questions.question: In December 2024, Pooja Sharma was named among BBC’s 100 Most Inspiring Women. What remarkable social service is she known for?

options.text: Performing last rites for unclaimed bodies

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Performing last rites for unclaimed bodies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pooja Sharma** was included in **BBC's 100 Most Inspiring Women** in **December 2024** for her exceptional contributions to society.
 
• She is widely recognized for her work in **performing last rites for unclaimed bodies**, ensuring dignity in death for the neglected and abandoned.
 
• Her initiatives involve identifying unclaimed bodies, completing legal formalities, and conducting respectful cremation or burial rites.
 
• Pooja collaborates with local authorities, hospitals, and NGOs to carry out this humanitarian work effectively and ethically.
 
• Her efforts aim to bring attention to the plight of unclaimed bodies and encourage societal responsibility towards the deceased.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unclaimed Bodies:**

 
 
• Unclaimed bodies are those found without any identifiable relatives or guardians to claim them.
 
• They are often the result of homelessness, estrangement, or unidentified accidents.
 
• Legal procedures are typically followed to determine the next steps, including post-mortem examinations and public notices.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Last Rites:**
 
 
• Last rites are rituals performed to honor the deceased and provide closure to their souls, as per various religious or cultural traditions.
 
• In many societies, performing last rites is considered essential for ensuring peace in the afterlife.
 
• For unclaimed bodies, these rites restore their dignity and humanity, regardless of their social status.
 
 
 
• **Humanitarian Efforts:**
 
 
• Individuals like Pooja Sharma play a critical role in addressing societal neglect and abandonment.
 
• Such efforts highlight the importance of compassion and inclusivity in society.
 
• Organizations and volunteers often work in collaboration to support these initiatives.
 
 
 
• **BBC 100 Women:**
 
 
• The BBC's 100 Women list celebrates influential and inspiring women globally.
 
• It highlights the contributions of women in various fields, including social work, science, arts, and activism.
 
• The initiative aims to recognize and amplify the voices of women making a difference.

questions.question: In March 2025, which Indian state experienced violent clashes resulting in multiple injuries over demands to remove the tomb of Mughal emperor Aurangzeb?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In March 2025, Maharashtra witnessed violent clashes over demands to remove the tomb of Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.
 
• The clashes occurred in the town of Khuldabad, Aurangabad district, where the tomb is located.
 
• Protesters demanded the removal of the tomb, claiming that it symbolizes a controversial legacy of Aurangzeb's rule.
 
• The incident led to multiple injuries and heightened communal tensions, prompting the deployment of additional police forces to maintain order.
 
• The Maharashtra government called for restraint and emphasized the need for peaceful resolution of the issue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aurangzeb's Tomb:**

 
 
• Located in Khuldabad, Maharashtra, this modest tomb reflects Aurangzeb's wish for simplicity in death.
 
• Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor, ruled from 1658 to 1707 and is a polarizing historical figure.
 
 
 
• **Khuldabad:**

• In September 2024, the Indian government formed a high-level committee to explore the feasibility and implementation of the 'One Nation, One Election' proposal.
 
• The committee is chaired by **Ram Nath Kovind**, the former President of India.
 
• The 'One Nation, One Election' proposal aims to synchronize elections for the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, Panchayats, and Urban Local Bodies to reduce electoral costs and disruptions.
 
• Ram Nath Kovind was chosen to lead this effort due to his experience and knowledge of constitutional and governance matters.
 
• This initiative reflects the government's intention to streamline electoral processes and improve governance efficiency in the country.

• **One Nation, One Election:**

 
 
• It is a proposal to hold simultaneous elections for Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, and local bodies to ensure uniformity and reduce frequent disruptions caused by election processes.
 
• The concept aims to save resources, both financial and administrative, while maintaining the focus on governance.
 
• Implementing this proposal requires significant constitutional amendments and consensus among political parties.
 
 
 
• **Ram Nath Kovind:**

• **Constitutional Amendments:**

• It would also necessitate changes to Representation of People Act, 1951.
 
 
 
• **Previous Discussions:**

questions.question: Who received a Special Citation in the 2025 Pulitzer Prizes for civil rights journalism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chuck Stone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chuck Stone received a Special Citation in the 2025 Pulitzer Prizes for his outstanding contributions to **civil rights journalism**.
 
• Stone was a pioneering African American journalist who played a significant role in **highlighting racial injustices** through his investigative reporting and editorials.
 
• He was a prominent figure in civil rights journalism, often using his platform to advocate for **equality and social justice**.
 
• Stone's work was recognized for its **courage, integrity, and impact** in shaping public discourse on civil rights issues in the United States.
 
• The Pulitzer Special Citation acknowledges exceptional contributions in journalism or arts that go beyond the standard categories recognized by the Pulitzer Board.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About the Pulitzer Prizes**

 
 
• The Pulitzer Prizes are annual awards for achievements in journalism, literature, and musical composition.
 
• Established in 1917 by provisions in the will of Joseph Pulitzer, a Hungarian-American newspaper publisher.
 
• They are administered by Columbia University and are considered one of the most prestigious honors in the fields they cover.
 
 
 
• **Special Citations in the Pulitzer Prizes**
 
 
• Special Citations are awarded at the discretion of the Pulitzer Board to individuals or organizations whose achievements do not fall into the regular categories.
 
• They often honor groundbreaking contributions in journalism, arts, or public service.
 
 
 
• **Chuck Stone's Legacy**
 
 
• Chuck Stone was one of the first African American columnists in the United States and a fierce advocate for civil rights.
 
• He worked for notable publications such as the Philadelphia Daily News and was a founding member of the National Association of Black Journalists (NABJ).
 
• Stone also wrote books and taught journalism at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Civil Rights Journalism**
 
 
• Civil rights journalism plays a crucial role in exposing systemic injustices and advocating for equality.
 
• It amplifies marginalized voices and ensures accountability for those in positions of power.
 
• Journalists like Chuck Stone have been instrumental in driving social change and promoting public awareness.
